To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) the savings behavior of agents is not a function of income or wealth, and (ii) the savings factor is determined by the agents’ perception of the market.
the savings behavior of agents can be explained by the following models.

(a) the reinforcement choice model is equivalent to the usual kinetic exchange model, (b) the strategic choice model is also equivalent to the usual model, but only when the agent's utility is a linear function of the income, and (c) the usual kinetic exchange is equivalent to the strategic choice model, if the agent's utility has a logarithmic dependence on income
In summary, our research is concerned with
the savings behavior of agents and the impact of such behavior on the income/wealth distributions.
developing a better understanding of the savings behavior of agents and its impact on the income/wealth distributions in the economy.
the development of a theory that explains the savings behavior of agents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the savings behavior can be explained in terms of the agents' preferences, their expectations, and the market conditions.
savings behavior of agents is determined by the relative income and the wealth of the individual agent and the average income and the average wealth of the population.
the kinetic exchange models with the reinforcement choice model are more appropriate for explaining the savings behavior of agents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the savings factor in the kinetic exchange model of market is a result of a combination of the following: (i) The agents' preferences, (ii) The agents' perception of their current and future income, (iii) The agents' risk aversion, and (iv) The agents' strategic behavior.
the savings factor of an agent depends on his/her wealth, the wealth of the other agents, and the wealth distribution of the economy.
the savings behavior of agents is determined by a complex interplay of the agents’ expectations and their past experiences.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the savings behavior of an agent is a result of the interplay between its own preferences and the social norms.
the kinetic exchange models can be used to model the savings behavior of individuals in the market.
the choice of savings function is not unique and depends on the model one uses to describe the economy.
